title: Digital Ethiopia 2025: online payments restricted by lack of financial interoperability
claim: Ethiopia's Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy states that online payments are restricted due to lack of interoperability among banks and financial services, that interoperability for financial transactions is in a nascent stage and currently limited overwhelmingly to analogue inter-banking transactions, and that mobile wallet services lack interoperability too.
evidence_summary: The strategy's digital payments sub-sector section reports that online payments are restricted due to lack of interoperability among banks and financial services, that interoperability for financial transactions is in a nascent stage and currently limited overwhelmingly to analogue inter-banking transactions requiring physical presence and paper forms, and that mobile wallet services - while a positive step - are unfortunately also lacking interoperability.
source_excerpt: Online payments are restricted due to lack of interoperability among banks and financial services. Interoperability for financial transactions is in a nascent stage and currently is limited overwhelmingly to analogue inter-banking transactions. These transactions require the customer to be physically present in the bank office as well as filling paper forms. While banks are implementing mobile wallet services - a positive step forward - they are also unfortunately lacking interoperability too.
interpretation: Policy evidence (government's own account) that financial-sector interoperability in Ethiopia is nascent, with direct consequences for digital payments. A government self-assessment; evidence of stated interoperability gaps and their effects, not an independent measurement.
citation: Ministry of Innovation and Technology, 'Digital Ethiopia 2025: A Digital Strategy for Ethiopia Inclusive Prosperity', digital payments sub-sector section (PDF p.59).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from the national digital strategy (digital payments sub-sector section). Publication date not independently verified.
keywords: interoperability, digital payments, mobile wallets, banks, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/5/digital-ethiopia-2025-strategy-english.pdf); page locator verified against the PDF's internal page marker (p.59).

title: Digital Ethiopia 2025: no regulation of data centres; in-house data centres and poor management acknowledged
claim: Ethiopia's Digital Ethiopia 2025 strategy states that there is no regulation of data centres in Ethiopia, that many public and private organizations have set up in-house data centres, and that the lack of regulation and certification of data centres results in poor management, especially of physical security.
evidence_summary: The strategy's cloud and data infrastructure section reports that there is no regulation of data centres, that many public and private organizations have set up in-house data centres, and that lack of regulation and certification results in poor management of these centres, especially physical security ensuring data is protected from theft or damage, and sets out plans to develop a data-centre strategy and standards.
source_excerpt: No regulation of data centres. Many public and private organizations have setup in-house data centres. However, lack of regulation and certification of data centres results in poor management of these centres, especially physical security, that ensures data is protected from theft or damage from natural disasters and environmental factors, like fire, flood and other factors.
interpretation: Policy evidence (government's own account) of the operational and regulatory state of data infrastructure in Ethiopia, relevant to the physical storage/residency side of data localization. A government self-assessment; evidence of stated gaps in data-centre governance, not an independent audit.
citation: Ministry of Innovation and Technology, 'Digital Ethiopia 2025: A Digital Strategy for Ethiopia Inclusive Prosperity', cloud and data infrastructure section (PDF p.62).
methodology_or_basis: Direct quote from the national digital strategy (cloud and data infrastructure section). Publication date not independently verified.
keywords: data centres, cloud, data governance, data residency, Ethiopia
notes: Real corpus record. Text extracted from acquired PDF (data/raw/5/digital-ethiopia-2025-strategy-english.pdf); page locator verified against the PDF's internal page marker (p.62).
